text:
Marissa Cole: Trying to close out the PRD section on roles. For enterprise: are we committing to *custom roles* at RBAC v2 GA, or are we shipping w/ just default roles (Org Admin, Billing Admin, Security Admin, Dev, Read-only, Support) and custom roles later?

Marissa Cole: Concern: a couple prospects keep asking “can I create a role that can export audit logs but can’t touch billing / SSO.” Default roles may not be enough. But custom roles can balloon UX + support.

Naomi Feldman: Yeah this is the big fork. Current eng plan for v0.1 policy bundle is default roles only. Custom roles is a separate UI + policy write-path + governance.

Naomi Feldman: We can still meet a lot of the enterprise questionnaires with default roles + SoD + auditability. But some customers will want that one-off mix.

Markus Klein: From SE side: I’d expect at least 2-3 deals to block on custom roles in the next quarter. Not every customer, but regulated ones do. They’re used to AWS/IAM style least privilege.

Marcus Lin: Security POV: I’m ok with phased approach as long as default roles are *tight* and we don’t create “god role” patterns. Also, if we do custom roles, we need guardrails + audit events for role changes.

Tessa Morgan: UX implication is non-trivial. If we do custom roles: we need permission catalog UI, grouping, search, warnings, “high risk” badges, and sane defaults.

Tessa Morgan: If we do default-only at GA, we can design the screens with a “Custom roles (coming soon)” stub and keep the mental model simpler.

Olga Petrov: For SOC 2 evidence: default roles are fine IF we can show (1) separation of duties options (2) audit logs for role assignment changes (3) admin review process. Custom roles adds extra controls to document.

Marissa Cole: What about “role templates” vs true custom roles? E.g., pre-defined additional roles beyond the 5-6 defaults.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: From implementation: policy engine can support arbitrary role definitions; the missing piece is role management lifecycle (create/update/delete) + policy distribution + validation.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: In Hosted we can store custom role defs per org. In Private we need to think about how those defs travel (customer control plane DB vs policy bundle?). That’s not in the 8-12 week plan.

Ethan Park: +1. Also migration complexity: if we add custom roles mid-migration, it complicates shadow mode comparisons (v1->v2) and support tooling.

Marissa Cole: So maybe: Phase 1 GA = default roles only, but we offer an “enterprise override” process where Security Eng can ship an additional role mapping for a specific customer?

Marcus Lin: I’d rather avoid bespoke policies getting hand-edited. That’s risky + hard to audit. But we can do a controlled “additional managed roles” program: customer requests → security review → we add a new template role into the bundle version and roll it out.

Olga Petrov: Managed roles via versioned policy bundle is cleaner for evidence. It’s basically “we provide pre-approved roles; changes follow change control.”

Markus Klein: That could work for early enterprise. But we need a crisp answer for “can we do custom roles” in the sales cycle.

Naomi Feldman: Proposed messaging:
- RBAC v2 GA includes: default roles + SSO group mapping to those roles + audit logs for role/permission changes.
- Custom roles: on roadmap; we can support a limited set of additional managed roles in the interim for enterprise.

Marissa Cole: Tessa, does that create awkward UI? Like customer sees role list and asks “why can’t I create one?”

Tessa Morgan: We can handle it. In Roles page:
- “Built-in roles” section.
- If customer is on Enterprise plan, show a disabled “Create role” button with tooltip “Coming soon” OR “Contact support to enable managed roles.”

Tessa Morgan: But we need to be careful not to imply they can self-serve custom roles if we can’t.

Elliot Price: Docs angle: we need to keep terminology consistent. “Custom roles” vs “managed roles” vs “role templates” will confuse people.

Elliot Price: If we do the interim thing, I’d call it “Additional built-in roles (by request)” and avoid “custom” anywhere until it’s self-serve.

Marissa Cole: Makes sense. Another Q: do we *need* to support “deny” semantics for custom roles? Some customers ask for explicit denies.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Current ADR direction is allow-only with deny-overrides reserved for internal/system policies. For customer-defined roles, allow-only is simpler (and less foot-gun). Explicit deny makes debugging rough.

Marcus Lin: +1. Allow-only reduces risk. We can still meet least privilege by not granting. Deny is mostly helpful when you have broad wildcard grants.

Naomi Feldman: Also: permission groupings matter. If we ship default roles only, we can avoid exposing the full permission catalog UI for now.

Markus Klein: But even w/ default roles, enterprise will ask “what does Security Admin actually include?” We need a readable matrix.

Marissa Cole: We have the role definitions doc, but console should show something too.

Tessa Morgan: Agreed. For GA: each role has “View permissions” drawer. It’s read-only but transparent. Include warnings like “Includes: SSO configuration, audit log exports, break-glass approvals” etc.

Olga Petrov: Please ensure it includes audit log export as a distinct permission. CISO asked for stricter default around exporting.

Marcus Lin: Yep. Export is sensitive; should not be in Developer or Billing Admin.

Ethan Park: Just to sanity check: is audit log export a console-only thing or API too? If it’s API, we need to include in the permission inventory and ensure enforcement in both control plane and console backend.

Naomi Feldman: Both. Kevin is updating audit exporter / schema. We’ll make `audit.logs.export` an explicit action.

Marissa Cole: Ok, so decision draft:
1) RBAC v2 GA: default roles only.
2) Enterprise interim: “additional built-in roles by request” via policy bundle updates (no per-customer bespoke policies).
3) UX: show built-in roles + permission viewer; no create role button (or disabled with “coming soon” depending on plan).
4) Roadmap: self-serve custom roles in a later phase.

Marissa Cole: Any objections?

Marcus Lin: Works for me if we document the interim request flow + approvals. (We should treat it like a security change.)

Olga Petrov: +1. I’ll add this as a note in control mapping / evidence expectations.

Tessa Morgan: +1, I’ll update designs to include “View permissions” and the copy for “additional roles by request.”

Markus Klein: Fine, but I need a sales-ready one-liner. “Custom roles not yet self-serve; we offer built-in least-privilege roles and can add additional role templates for enterprise as needed.”

Elliot Price: I’ll align docs language and add an FAQ for “Do you support custom roles?” with the phased answer.

Naomi Feldman: I’ll drop a comment on PM-912 with this decision + open a follow-up ticket for “additional built-in roles request workflow” so it doesn’t get lost.

Marissa Cole: Cool. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

(reactions: Marcus Lin :thumbsup:, Tessa Morgan :white_check_mark:, Olga Petrov :thumbsup:)
